description:
crate-jmap-server/src/parse.rs:63 — parse_request signature is:

    pub fn parse_request(body: Value, max_calls: usize) -> Result<JmapRequest, JmapError>

`body: Value` means the JSON parse has already happened in the
caller's code by the time parse_request runs. The function's own
doc comment (parse.rs:28-55) acknowledges this and lays out a long
caller-responsibility list:

- Caller must enforce HTTP body byte-size limit before parsing.
- Caller must use `serde_json::from_slice` (or equivalent) with the
  serde_json recursion limit honored.
- Caller "should consider rejecting request bodies that exceed ~32
  levels of JSON nesting".

The runtime cost of these obligations is high: serde_json's default
recursion limit is 128, well above the documented "32 levels
comfortably exceeds any legitimate JMAP request shape". A naive
consumer that does `let body: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)?`
already eats up to 128 levels of stack before parse_request runs.

What callers cannot depend on: that calling parse_request is
sufficient for safe JMAP request handling. The function's name and
position suggest "do this and you're protected"; the doc says
"actually do these three other things first, only one of which is
covered by a default crate behaviour".

What goes wrong when this stays as-is: consumers cargo-cult the
example in README.md ("parse_request(body_json, /* max_calls */ 16)")
without reading the full doc, and ship a server that stack-overflows
on a 200-level adversarial nested JSON. The kit's defenses for
ResultReference path depth (MAX_JSON_POINTER_DEPTH = 32 in parse.rs)
and merge patch depth (MAX_MERGE_PATCH_DEPTH = 32 in helpers.rs) do
not fire because they are downstream of the JSON parse.

Resolution paths:

- Offer a `parse_request_bytes(body: &[u8], max_calls: usize) ->
  Result<JmapRequest, JmapError>` variant that does the JSON parse
  internally with a kit-controlled depth limit. Keep the existing
  Value-taking function for consumers that already have a Value
  (federation hand-off, test fixtures).

- Document the depth-limit obligation more prominently — surface it
  in README.md "How to use" rather than burying it in parse.rs
  doc.

- Ship an `enforce_json_depth(&serde_json::Value, max_depth: usize)`
  helper that walks an already-parsed Value to count depth, so
  consumers who have a Value can defend in depth.

The library-kit posture in workspace AGENTS.md is "consumer brings
HTTP, auth, persistence". The depth-cap obligation does fit that
posture in principle, but the doc-buried form invites footguns.
title: parse_request takes serde_json::Value not bytes — JSON-depth-cap responsibility unenforceable from inside the kit
